strings.d1.s0.name: Stortorget
strings.d1.s0.tips: Medieval square lined with colourful houses. Home to the Nobel Museum and the site of the 1520 bloodbath. Quiet in the morning.
strings.d1.s1.name: Royal Palace Stockholm
strings.d1.s1.tips: A 600-room palace: see the State Apartments and the Treasury, and catch the changing of the guard at 12:15 (mounted in summer).
strings.d1.s2.name: Under Kastanjen Gamla Stan
strings.d1.s2.tips: Courtyard café under chestnut trees. Try the meatballs and kanelbulle (cinnamon bun).
strings.d1.s3.name: Mårten Trotzigs Gränd & Prästgatan
strings.d1.s3.tips: The narrowest alley, just 90 cm wide. Look for the rune stone, and escape the tourist crowds of Västerlånggatan.
strings.d1.s4.name: Riddarholmen Church & Monteliusvägen
strings.d1.s4.tips: Royal tombs (summer), then a sunset view of Gamla Stan from the Södermalm cliffs.
strings.d1.b0.name: Nobel Prize Museum
strings.d1.b0.tips: See the Nobel chairs, signed underneath. Swap in for the street wandering.
strings.d1.b1.name: Kaffekoppen Stortorget
strings.d1.b1.tips: Café on the square; time for fika (coffee break).
strings.d2.s0.name: Vasa Museum
strings.d2.s0.tips: A 69 m warship that sank on its maiden voyage in 1628 (98% original). One of the world's best museums; opens at 09:00.
strings.d2.s1.name: Skansen
strings.d2.s1.tips: The world's first open-air museum (1891). Swedish village houses, elk, reindeer, wolves, and dancing in summer.
strings.d2.s2.name: Skansen Solliden Restaurant
strings.d2.s2.tips: Restaurant with a view inside Skansen; try the meatballs.
strings.d2.s3.name: ABBA The Museum
strings.d2.s3.tips: Sing on stage with ABBA. Timed tickets, book online.
strings.d2.s4.name: Rosendals Trädgård
strings.d2.s4.tips: Garden café and bakery with an apple orchard and kanelbulle. Outdoor seating in summer.
strings.d2.b0.name: Nordic Museum
strings.d2.b0.tips: Scandinavian way of life, including Sami culture. Swap in for ABBA.
strings.d2.b1.name: Blå Porten Djurgården
strings.d3.s0.name: Fotografiska
strings.d3.s0.tips: Photography museum in a former customs house. The rooftop café overlooks the harbour, and it stays open until 23:00.
strings.d3.s1.name: Nytorget & SoFo
strings.d3.s1.tips: Hipster Södermalm: vintage shops and Greta Garbo's old neighbourhood.
strings.d3.s2.name: Meatballs for the People
strings.d3.s2.tips: 14 kinds of meatballs (including elk and reindeer) in SoFo.
strings.d3.s3.name: Skinnarviksberget
strings.d3.s3.tips: The city's highest natural point, with views over Riddarfjärden. Good for a picnic.
strings.d3.s4.name: Mariaberget & Monteliusvägen Sunset
strings.d3.s4.tips: Cliffside walking path with sunset views of City Hall and Gamla Stan.
strings.d3.b0.name: Pelikan Södermalm
strings.d3.b1.name: Spritmuseum Djurgården
strings.d3.b1.tips: Museum of snaps and aquavit. Swap in for Fotografiska.
strings.d4.s0.name: Stockholm City Hall
strings.d4.s0.tips: The Nobel banquet is held in the Blue Hall, with mosaics in the Golden Hall. Tour is compulsory; the tower (summer) is 106 m.
strings.d4.s1.name: Drottningholm Palace
strings.d4.s1.tips: Home of the royal family (UNESCO), with a baroque garden and the Chinese Pavilion. Take the 1-hour boat from Stadshuskajen (summer) or the metro and bus.
strings.d4.s2.name: Drottningholm Palace Theatre
strings.d4.s2.tips: 1766 baroque theatre with original stage machinery. Guided tour.
strings.d4.s3.name: Drottningholms Paviljong Café
strings.d4.s3.tips: Café in the palace gardens: smörgås (open sandwich) and fika.
strings.d4.s4.name: Lovön Island Walk
strings.d4.s4.tips: Walk along the shore of Lake Mälaren. Return by boat or bus.
strings.d4.b0.name: Millesgården Lidingö
strings.d4.b0.tips: Terraced garden museum of the sculptor Carl Milles. Swap in for Drottningholm.
strings.d4.b1.name: Stadshuskällaren
strings.d4.b1.tips: Nobel menu (from past years) in the City Hall cellar.
strings.d5.s0.name: Waxholmsbolaget Strömkajen
strings.d5.s0.tips: Archipelago ferry (30,000 islands). Vaxholm takes 1 hour; the Båtluffarkortet 5-day pass costs 995 SEK.
strings.d5.s1.name: Vaxholm Fortress
strings.d5.s1.tips: Island fortress and museum, plus the town's wooden houses.
strings.d5.s2.name: Vaxholms Hembygdsgård Café
strings.d5.s2.tips: Seaside café; try the prawn sandwich (räksmörgås).
strings.d5.s3.name: Grinda Island
strings.d5.s3.tips: Nature reserve island: swim off the rocks (summer), hike, and eat at Grinda Wärdshus. Return ferry at 18:00.
strings.d5.b0.name: Fjäderholmarna
strings.d5.b0.tips: The island closest to the city, 20 minutes away, with craftspeople and a restaurant.
strings.d5.b1.name: Grinda Wärdshus
strings.d6.s0.name: Östermalms Saluhall
strings.d6.s0.tips: 1888 gourmet food hall: fish at Lisa Elmqvist, and fika.
strings.d6.s1.name: Uppsala Cathedral
strings.d6.s1.tips: 40 minutes by train. Scandinavia's largest cathedral, with the tomb of Gustav Vasa and Linnaeus.
strings.d6.s2.name: Gustavianum & University
strings.d6.s3.name: Güntherska Hovkonditori Uppsala
strings.d6.s3.tips: 1870 pastry shop; try prinsesstårta (princess cake with green marzipan).
strings.d6.s4.name: Gamla Uppsala
strings.d6.s4.tips: Viking royal burial mounds and a museum. Take bus 2, then the train back.
strings.d6.b0.name: Sigtuna
strings.d6.b0.tips: Sweden's oldest town (980), with rune stones. Swap in for Uppsala.
strings.d6.b1.name: Hambergs Fisk Uppsala
strings.d7.s0.name: Rålambshovsparken
strings.d7.s0.tips: Waterfront park with views of Västerbron bridge.
strings.d7.s1.name: Vete-Katten
strings.d7.s1.tips: 1928 pastry shop: kanelbulle and semla (February), for a farewell fika.
strings.d7.s2.name: Drottninggatan & Sergels Torg
strings.d7.s2.tips: Pedestrian shopping street. Visit NK and Kulturhuset, and pick up a Dala horse as a souvenir.
strings.d7.s3.name: Arlanda Express Centralen
strings.d7.s3.tips: 20-minute express train. Time to say goodbye.
strings.d7.b0.name: Hallwyl Museum
strings.d7.b0.tips: Free 1898 palace-home. Swap in for shopping.
strings.d7.b1.name: Café Pascal Norrmalm
strings.note0: The SL card lasts 72 hours and covers tram 7 to Djurgården and the ferry. Arlanda Express costs 340 SEK (Flygbussarna 130). Cash is not accepted; cards (Swish) are used everywhere.
strings.note1: Summer temperatures are 20-25°C, with daylight from 04:00 to 22:00. At Midsummer (the 3rd Friday of June) everything closes, though Skansen celebrates. You can swim in the archipelago, and boats run to Drottningholm.
strings.note2: Meatballs cost 200 SEK, fika 80-110, restaurants 300-500, museums 150-280. For a tip, round up the bill. The city is expensive, so work out whether the Stockholm Pass (Go City) pays off for museums.
strings.note3: Arrive at Vasa when it opens at 09:00. ABBA tickets are timed and booked online, and the City Hall tour is compulsory. In summer, take the boat to Drottningholm (1 hour); it is a pleasant trip.
strings.note4: Fika culture: kanelbulle (on 4 October, the Cinnamon Bun Day!), kardemummabulle (cardamom bun), prinsesstårta; smörgåsbord, gravlax, and surströmming (fermented herring, for the brave).
strings.note5: Systembolaget (the state liquor store) closes at 20:00 and is shut on Sundays. A beer in a bar costs 80 SEK.
strings.transit.name: SL 72-hour pass + optional Stockholm Pass
strings.transit.why_chosen: Covers metro, bus, tram 7 and the Djurgården ferry; 72 hours costs about 350 SEK
